report:
Based on this research, here is my conclusion:

## Conclusion

**Yes—EMDR is an effective, evidence-based treatment that alleviates PTSD symptoms**, with efficacy generally comparable to trauma-focused cognitive-behavioral therapy (TF-CBT), one of the other leading treatments for the condition.

Multiple systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials confirm this. A 2023 meta-analysis in *Psicothema* found EMDR produced substantial symptom reduction across studies from 1991–2022 (pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37882423/). Broader summaries note that a 38-RCT meta-analysis found a large effect size (SMD ≈ –1.07) for EMDR versus no treatment, and 24 RCTs comparing EMDR to CBT found equivalent efficacy, with EMDR often requiring fewer sessions and having lower dropout rates in some trials (e.g., 6% vs. 29% in a veteran study comparing EMDR to prolonged exposure) (gitnux.org/emdr-statistics/). The Wikipedia summary of the literature similarly states that post-2013 analyses generally show EMDR's efficacy is equivalent to TF-CBT approaches like prolonged exposure and cognitive processing therapy (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_movement_desensitization_and_reprocessing).

This evidence is reinforced by major clinical and public-health authorities: the World Health Organization's 2013 guidelines for conditions related to stress explicitly recommend EMDR for adults, adolescents, and children with PTSD (who.int/news/item/06-08-2013-who-releases-guidance-on-mental-health-care-after-trauma). The American Psychological Association's Clinical Practice Guideline for PTSD in adults also lists EMDR as a recommended psychotherapy option (apa.org/ptsd-guideline/treatments/eye-movement-reprocessing).

**Bottom line:** EMDR has strong, consistent research support and endorsement from major health organizations as an effective PTSD treatment, on par with other first-line trauma-focused therapies.
